If results are found, they are displayed in the 'search_results' element. If a non-existing webpage is requested, a generic whitelabel error page is displayed with an error type of 'Not Found' and a status of 404.} [completed]

nodes.title: 2.1 Analyze Spring Data MongoDB - {Findings: Spring Data MongoDB simplifies integration of Spring applications with MongoDB, but has vulnerabilities, especially involving injection. The primary vulnerability is CVE-2022-22980, a Spring Expression Language (SpEL) injection vulnerability. This vulnerability, with a CVSS score of 9.8, affects applications that use repository query methods annotated with `@Query` or `@Aggregation`, especially when these methods use SpEL expressions with query parameter placeholders for value binding and the user input is not properly sanitized. The vulnerability arises when an application invokes a query method with non-sanitized user input. Successful exploitation can lead to arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the Spring MongoDB process. An application is vulnerable if it meets several conditions, including use of `@Query` or `@Aggregation`, use of SpEL parts using the parameter placeholder syntax within the expression, user-supplied input is not sanitized, and certain versions of Spring Data MongoDB are used. Mitigation includes updating Spring Data MongoDB to patched versions, sanitizing user input, using array syntax for parameters, implementing custom repository methods, and limiting SpEL usage. General NoSQL injection principles apply when interacting with MongoDB. MongoDB queries are typically JSON-like objects. If user input is directly inserted into these queries without validation or sanitation, an attacker can inject malicious operators or values. General prevention for MongoDB includes using parameterized queries/ORMs, validating and sanitizing input, restricting user privileges, avoiding unsafe query operators, and regularly updating dependencies. References and further reading include the official Spring advisory for CVE-2022-22980, the Snyk vulnerability database, an article on The Daily Swig, the OWASP Cheat Sheet Series for NoSQL Injection Prevention, and MongoDB security documentation. The MongoDB official documentation provides comprehensive security features and best practices for securing deployments. The Spring Data MongoDB Project Page provides official documentation and links to releases. There are several articles discussing general prevention strategies for MongoDB injection attacks.} [to_do]
